summary: Elizabeth Errington works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS and under Adrian David Hugh Bivar, later holding posts at the British Museum, the British Institute of Persian Studies, the Fitzwilliam Museum, and the University of Oxford.

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Canterbury and served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago, where she was attested in 2007.

Elizabeth J. Harris works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate under Ananda Guruge and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and University of Kelaniya, later holding posts at Westminster College and Birmingham.

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan and held academic posts at the University of Washington (circa 1979–1990) and Harvard University (circa 1997).

Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at Stanford under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, also studying under Janet Gyatso and Susan Niditch, and held posts at Amherst College and Middlebury College.

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Paul Groner, and Geshe Wangyal, and served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project.
Elizabeth Rohlman specializes in Indology and religious studies. She has held posts at the University of Calgary, where she is attested in 2014 and attested as Associate Head in 2026.
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality. She served as Direktorin at the University of Winchester in 2021.
Elke Rogersdotter is an archaeologist and Indologist. She completed her PhD at Umeå University, where she was supervised by Thomas B. Larsson, Bozena Werbart, Karin Viklund, and P. Ajithprasad.
Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She held editorial posts with the International Institute for Asian Studies, Leiden University, and Gonda Indological Studies.

Elliot M. Stern is an Indologist who earned his doctorates at the University of Pennsylvania. He studied under George Cardona, Wilhelm Halbfass, Ludo Rocher, and traditional teacher P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri.

Elliot Sperling was a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Lynn Struve, later holding faculty posts at Indiana University, Southern Mississippi, Harvard, and Delhi.
Ellison Banks Findly works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Fred Pfeil and held positions at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford.

Ellwood Austin Welden was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania, and held posts at Bryn Mawr College, the Lawrenceville School, the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce, and the University of Maine.

Elmer Henry Cutts was an Indologist and historian. He earned degrees from the University of Washington and Harvard University, and held posts at the University of Washington, Tufts University, and Northeastern University, later founding Andhra University in 1958.
Elof Olesen was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed an M.A. at the University of Copenhagen between 1895 and 1903, where he studied under Michael Viggo Fausbøll.

Elpidius Pax worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied under Wilhelm Havers and Otto Strauss at the University of Breslau, earning degrees there and at Munich, and later held professorships at the Studium Biblicum Franciscanum and Dormition Abbey.
Else Lüders was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Heinrich Lüders and received an honorary doctorate from the University of Rostock in 1919.

Else Pauly was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the University of Copenhagen under Louis Trolle Hjelmslev and Poul Tuxen, later serving there as a part-time lecturer in Pāli from 1973 to 1979.

Else Wohlgemuth was a scholar of Indology and sinology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Marburg, and the University of Leipzig, where she earned her PhD under Ernst Windisch.
